1. Scope — This standard specifies the materials, dimensions and other requirements for sand- 
wich bread moulds. 

2. Definitions 

2.1 Sandwich Bread — A flat top bread, baked in a mould with cover. 

3. IVIaterials 

3.1 The body of the moulds shall be made from tinplate of minimum 0*54 mm thickness. Tinplate 
may be hot-dipped or electrolytic type having tm coatmg mass A 14/14 and E 1 1*2/1 1*2 respec- 
tively [ 5ee IS : 1993-1982 Specification for cold-reduced tinplate and cold-reduced blackplate 
( second revision ) ] . 

3.2 Galvanized wire of 40 mm diameter shall be used for strengthening of top edges. 

4* Dimensions — The dimensions for 200, 400 and 800 g loaf moulds shall be as given in 
Table 1 and Fig. 1.

5. Worlcmanship and Finish 

5.1 Moulds shall be manufactured by rivetting or spot welding. In case of rivetting, heads shall 
not protrude. 

5.2 The moulds shall have a smooth surface and shall be smoothly finished, free from cracks and 
projections. 

6 Lids — Lids shall be made of cold rolled cold annealed ( CRCA ) sheets or tinplate of 
0-54 mm minimum thickness to slide fit on the mould. 

7. Packing and IVIarking 

7.1 Packing — The sandwich bread moulds shall be packed suitably to prevent damage in 
transit. 

7.2 Marking — The sandwich bread moulds shall be indelibly and legibly marked with the 
following: 

a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark, and 

b) Capaqity and dimensions of the mould.

7.2.1 Standard Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

8, Sampling — The representative samples of the sandwich bread moulds shall be drawn as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Sandwich bread moulds of different materials and dimensions are being manufactured 
in the country. In this standard only tinplate has been specified for use. However, in view of the 
shortage of tinplate, alternate materials are being investigated, such as utensil or food grade 
aluminium and its alloys. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of thjs standard is complied 
with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960 'Rules for rounded of numerical values ( revised Y^ 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard.
